Information since May points to continued labor-market strength and solid growth with inflation near 2 percent, supporting the Committee’s decision to raise rates and signal further gradual normalization. Incorporating the April 2018 SLOOS: banks reported policy changes and softer conditions in commercial real estate alongside wider loan rate spreads—signs of mild tightening in credit pricing/availability—while residential mortgage standards (e.g., QM jumbos) were broadly unchanged. Foreign banks reported ongoing demand and borrower inquiries for CRE and C&I loans, suggesting credit demand remains present even as pricing tightens. Net effect: the macro tone remains moderately positive with a cautious, slightly tighter credit backdrop, tempering the earlier enthusiasm modestly.
